title: Seerah
description: General User → Pro. Familiar events from the Prophet’s life, broader basics and short everyday applications requiring deeper understanding of context. Covers opposition, the Hijrah, community life, major events, teaching, consideration and responsible leadership. All questions are Pro level within the General User audience; obscure dates, specialist historical disputes and reference-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Pro describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires deeper understanding, connecting familiar teachings and distinguishing common misconceptions beyond Mid, without specialist study. This is General User Pro, not the separate Ultra bank. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What did Waraqah warn the Prophet about after hearing of the first revelation?

options.text: His people would oppose him and drive him out
Revelation guaranteed immediate public approval
He would never experience hardship again
His message would depend on inherited wealth

questions.explanation: Waraqah recognized a pattern of opposition faced by earlier messengers and offered support if he lived to see it.

questions.question: When warning his close relatives, what did the Prophet make clear?

options.text: Relatives had no responsibility for their actions
Family relationship alone could not save them from Allah's judgment
His family could replace faith with ancestry
Only strangers needed to heed the warning

questions.explanation: The Prophet addressed even his daughter and aunt, distinguishing family affection from exemption from accountability.

questions.question: What response did the Prophet give when Khabbab reported persecution?

options.text: He promised all hardship would end that afternoon
He said suffering made faith worthless
He recalled earlier believers' endurance and gave hope for the faith's future
He made social popularity the test of truth

questions.explanation: The report combines encouragement to remain steadfast with a warning against impatience over the expected outcome.

questions.question: What role did a skilled guide have in the Hijrah arrangements?

options.text: He replaced revelation as the source of faith
He was chosen because he knew no routes
He made all travel preparation unnecessary
He was hired and trusted to guide the journey

questions.explanation: The account describes an expert guide entrusted with transport and the route, despite not sharing the travelers' faith.

questions.question: Which change in prayer direction occurred during the Prophet's Madinan life?

options.text: From Jerusalem toward the Kabah in Makkah
From the Kabah toward Yemen
From Madinah toward Abyssinia
From prayer toward having no direction at all

questions.explanation: The report describes the change of qiblah and worshippers turning after receiving news of the Prophet's prayer.

questions.question: What about Al-Miqdad's statement delighted the Prophet before Badr?

options.text: His refusal to share any responsibility
His assurance that they would stand beside him
His claim that numbers made Allah's help unnecessary
His demand for personal praise before helping

questions.explanation: Al-Miqdad expressed committed support instead of leaving the Prophet to face the challenge without them.

questions.question: What misplaced confidence at Hunayn does the Quran recall?

options.text: Confidence that no preparation was ever needed
The belief that only small groups could succeed
Pride in great numbers that did not prevent the initial setback
The idea that the battle had no human participants

questions.explanation: The verse warns that impressive numbers alone were not sufficient protection against a setback.

questions.question: Which event does Anas identify with the Quran's announcement of a clear victory?

options.text: The death of the Prophet's son Ibrahim
The loss of Aishah's necklace
The change of qiblah in Madinah
The peace agreement at Hudaybiyyah

questions.explanation: Anas identifies Hudaybiyyah in explaining the verse. Another report describes the Prophet receiving the surah with joy.

questions.question: What did the Prophet visibly do during the reported Ramadan journey toward Makkah?

options.text: He drank water and broke his fast while traveling
He declared all Ramadan fasting permanently abolished
He required every resident to stop fasting
He taught that travelers could never fast

questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet both fasting and not fasting on journeys, illustrating the recognized travel concession.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet leave a proposed rebuilding of the Kabah uncarried out?

options.text: He had no knowledge of Ibrahim's foundations
His people's recent departure from the pre-Islamic period was a concern
He believed a beneficial change must always be rushed
He thought people's circumstances could never matter

questions.explanation: He explained the desired rebuilding to Aishah while identifying a reason for restraint in the circumstances.

questions.question: What warning accompanied the Prophet's instructions to Muadh about collecting zakah?

options.text: Take whatever the collector most admires
Treat authority as permission for personal gain
Avoid taking the best possessions and beware the wronged person's supplication
Ignore the rights of those paying

questions.explanation: The instructions join a religious duty with restraint and a warning against oppression in carrying it out.

questions.question: How did the Prophet address the Ansar's hurt after the Hunayn distribution?

options.text: He said their long service had no value
He refused to acknowledge their feelings at all
He measured their worth only by livestock received
He spoke to them and affirmed their closeness to him

questions.explanation: His address reminded the Ansar of their relationship and of returning home with him rather than merely with material goods.

questions.question: What protection did the Prophet emphasize in his Farewell Hajj address?

options.text: The sanctity of people's lives and property
Permission to harm others for tribal prestige
The removal of every duty toward others
The idea that pilgrimage excuses injustice

questions.explanation: Jabir's account records the address affirming the inviolability of life and property rather than leaving ethics outside worship.

questions.question: Which provision was revealed during the journey delayed by Aishah's lost necklace?

options.text: The abolition of purification before prayer
Tayammum when water was unavailable
The replacement of every prayer with charity
A rule that lost objects must never be searched for

questions.explanation: The report places the revelation about tayammum in this journey's lack of water. It is a specific historical account.

questions.question: What did the Prophet speak to the young Abu Umayr about?

options.text: His entitlement to public office
His rank among wealthy families
His little bird
His ability to solve every adult dispute

questions.explanation: Anas recalled the Prophet's approachable manner, including a warm question about his younger brother's bird.

questions.question: How did the Prophet guide the young Umar ibn Abi Salamah at a meal?

options.text: Eat faster to impress the adults
Stop asking every practical question
Treat manners as irrelevant in private
Mention Allah, use the right hand and eat what is near

questions.explanation: The boy remembered clear instructions given during an ordinary meal and continued to follow them.

questions.question: What did the Prophet do after learning that the person who cleaned the mosque had died?

options.text: Asked for the grave and offered funeral prayer there
Dismissed the person as unimportant
Said modest service could never deserve attention
Forbade anyone remembering the person's work

questions.explanation: The report shows his concern for someone whose death others had treated as of little importance.

questions.question: How did the Prophet respond when a poorly clothed group came in need?

options.text: He treated their need as entertainment
He urged charity and was pleased when help gathered
He waited for them to become influential
He praised concern while discouraging practical help

questions.explanation: Jarir describes the Prophet's concern, his appeal for charity and his joy when food and clothing were gathered.

questions.question: What description did the Prophet tell people to use while warning against exaggerated praise?

options.text: An equal partner in Allah's divinity
An independent source of all unseen knowledge
Allah's servant and messenger
A being beyond every human limitation

questions.explanation: The Prophet's own instruction keeps honor and love consistent with his servanthood and messengership.

questions.question: What central reminder did Abu Bakr give after the Prophet's death?

options.text: The Prophet's death ended every duty to Allah
Grief made revelation no longer relevant
The community should replace worship with ancestry
Muhammad had died, while Allah is ever-living and does not die

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr recalled the distinction between Allah and His messenger and recited Quranic guidance to the grieving community.

questions.question: Why does Waraqah's response challenge the idea that a true message always wins immediate approval?

options.text: He expected hostility toward a messenger bringing truth
He treated popularity as the proof of revelation
He promised there would be no opposition
He said any difficult mission must be abandoned

questions.explanation: The first-revelation account includes anticipated opposition, so immediate acceptance is not its measure of truth.

questions.question: What distinction appears in the Prophet's words to Fatimah about his wealth and Allah's judgment?

options.text: Material gifts automatically removed every spiritual responsibility
He could give material help without granting exemption from judgment
Being loved made obedience unnecessary
Family care and accountability could never coexist

questions.explanation: The report distinguishes what he could give from his property from a claim to independently save relatives from Allah's judgment.

questions.question: What does the Prophet's reassurance to Khabbab caution against?

options.text: Believing earlier people could endure difficulty
Keeping hope during suffering
Expecting a worthy cause to face no hardship or delay
Recognizing that patience can be needed

questions.explanation: The account encourages perseverance and warns against impatience. It does not make persecution acceptable or forbid seeking protection.

questions.question: What practical distinction does hiring the Hijrah guide illustrate?

options.text: Any shared task means adopting another person's entire belief
Faith makes route knowledge irrelevant
Only identical beliefs can ever accompany reliable practical work
Using trusted expertise is different from accepting someone's religious beliefs

questions.explanation: The guide was trusted for an ordinary professional task. This is not the same as making him a source of revelation.

questions.question: Why were prayers before the qiblah change not simply treated as wasted?

options.text: Worshippers had followed the direction prescribed at that time
A later change proves every earlier act was deliberate disobedience
Any prayer direction is always equally prescribed
Only prayers after the Prophet's death count

questions.explanation: The report recalls concern about earlier worshippers and the reassurance that Allah would not let their faith, meaning their prayers here, be lost.

questions.question: What distinguishes Al-Miqdad's encouragement from leaving a leader isolated?

options.text: He offered praise while refusing all involvement
He expressed willingness to share the challenge
He made support depend only on personal comfort
He demanded that one person carry every burden

questions.explanation: His assurance delighted the Prophet. The narrative illustrates committed support in its historical setting, rather than merely flattering words.

questions.question: What lesson about resources follows from the account of Hunayn?

options.text: Having more people always makes preparation unnecessary
The verse forbids every use of material resources
Resources do not guarantee success or remove dependence on Allah
A large group can never experience a setback

questions.explanation: The account corrects overconfidence in numbers. It does not say responsible preparation is forbidden.

questions.question: Why is judging Hudaybiyyah only by immediate disappointment incomplete?

options.text: Every disappointing agreement is necessarily identical to Hudaybiyyah
A negotiated outcome can never have value
The Prophet treated the revealed surah as unwelcome
The transmitted account identifies it as a clear victory

questions.explanation: The reports require considering the event beyond its first appearance. This does not automatically validate every difficult modern agreement.

questions.question: Why would saying the Prophet never broke a Ramadan fast while traveling be inaccurate?

options.text: The narration explicitly records him doing so
The report says he never traveled in Ramadan
Only companions could ever use the concession
Travel made Ramadan cease to exist

questions.explanation: The report records his public use of the concession and also mentions fasting on journeys. It does not establish that either choice fits every circumstance.

questions.question: What does the uncarried-out rebuilding illustrate about leadership?

options.text: Every possible improvement must happen immediately
A beneficial optional change may need consideration of people's circumstances
Considering consequences always means rejecting truth
A community's recent history can never matter

questions.explanation: The episode concerns a particular rebuilding decision. It does not give a general excuse to ignore obligations or leave injustice unaddressed.

questions.question: Why is collecting a religious obligation not permission to act oppressively?

options.text: A religious title removes all limits on collection
The collector's preference always defines what is owed
The Prophet explicitly attached safeguards against unfair taking
The payer loses every right once collection begins

questions.explanation: The instruction about zakah includes a limit on taking prized possessions and a warning concerning the oppressed.

questions.question: What does the address to the Ansar show about material share and belonging?

options.text: Receiving less always proved a person was despised
Their earlier service had become worthless
Every distribution decision should be copied without context
A distribution was not the sole measure of their closeness to the Prophet

questions.explanation: He affirmed their closeness. This particular distribution is not a universal formula for unrelated cases.

questions.question: Why is it incomplete to study the Farewell Hajj only as a sequence of rituals?

options.text: Its recorded address also emphasizes people's rights
The account replaces every ritual with trade
Pilgrimage makes moral duties disappear
The sermon treats people's property as irrelevant

questions.explanation: The same pilgrimage account includes both worship and strong instruction concerning life and property.

questions.question: What would go beyond the account of the lost necklace and tayammum?

options.text: Recognizing a historical occasion of revelation
Claiming every modern inconvenience can create a new religious rule
Noting that the travelers lacked water
Acknowledging the provision taught in the report

questions.explanation: Revelation during the Prophet's life is not equivalent to later people inventing rules because an inconvenience occurs.

questions.question: What does the conversation with Abu Umayr show about dignity and approachability?

options.text: Children mattered only if they discussed adult affairs
A leader's dignity required avoiding every warm conversation
A child's ordinary interests could receive the Prophet's attention
Only wealthy adults deserved personal attention

questions.explanation: The remembered conversation shows approachable warmth rather than treating a child's concerns as beneath notice.

questions.question: What teaching strength appears in the Prophet's advice at the meal?

options.text: A vague demand with no explanation of what to do
A requirement to master every rule before eating
Making the child guess which action needed changing
Specific guidance the learner could immediately apply

questions.explanation: The report gives concrete instructions tied to the situation, and Umar remembered continuing to follow them.

questions.question: Why is the mosque-cleaner's story a challenge to status-based attention?

options.text: The Prophet showed concern for someone others had overlooked
Only prestigious work was remembered
Quiet service made a person less worthy of consideration
A public title was necessary before anyone could matter

questions.explanation: His inquiry and funeral prayer demonstrate regard beyond social prominence or a highly visible role.

questions.question: How did the response to the needy group move beyond feeling sympathy?

options.text: The Prophet discouraged every practical contribution
Concern led to an appeal and actual provision of help
The group was told that appearances alone solved poverty
Only a public speech was permitted to count as care

questions.explanation: The narrative includes food and clothing gathered after the appeal. Compassion took practical form.

questions.question: Why does avoiding exaggerated praise not mean abandoning love for the Prophet?

options.text: Love requires granting him Allah's divinity
Every respectful description is forbidden
Honoring him should remain consistent with his own teaching
Affection automatically removes all limits on claims

questions.explanation: His instruction gives a way to honor him truthfully as Allah's servant and messenger.

questions.question: What does Abu Bakr's response show about grief and guidance?

options.text: The Prophet's death made all revelation void
Love required denying that the Prophet had died
Mourning made every responsibility permanently disappear
Profound loss did not end the community's duty to Allah

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr acknowledged the death while recalling Quranic guidance and the continuing worship of Allah.

questions.question: A reader says opposition to the Prophet proves his mission could not be true. Which part of the first-revelation account challenges this?

options.text: Waraqah expected hostility toward a true messenger
Waraqah promised immediate universal agreement
Khadijah treated public approval as revelation
The account denies that messengers faced resistance

questions.explanation: Waraqah's warning shows that opposition was anticipated. Opposition alone is not a test establishing or disproving a claim's truth.

questions.question: Someone claims a respected religious family makes their own conduct irrelevant. Which Prophetic warning applies?

options.text: Every relative inherited exemption from judgment
Even close relatives were told to take their responsibility before Allah seriously
Family affection replaced personal responsibility
Material gifts always settled spiritual accountability

questions.explanation: The Prophet's words to his relatives reject treating family connection as an independent guarantee of salvation.

questions.question: A summary says the Prophet's words to Khabbab ban every attempt to seek protection from persecution. What needs correcting?

options.text: The report makes persecution morally acceptable
It promises immediate relief to every reader
Encouragement to persevere is not a blanket ban on seeking protection
It says only comfort can accompany genuine faith

questions.explanation: The narration teaches steadfastness and hope. It should not be turned into an instruction to accept every preventable harm.

questions.question: A team needs a trustworthy, qualified guide for an ordinary lawful journey. Which lesson fits the Hijrah report?

options.text: Assume route knowledge is unnecessary when people have faith
Treat hiring someone as accepting all their beliefs
Choose only by impressive claims, without checking competence
Assess practical competence and trustworthiness without confusing the role with religious authority

questions.explanation: The migration account includes reliance on a skilled, trusted guide. The application concerns professional assistance, not authority over belief.

questions.question: A Seerah summary calls every prayer toward Jerusalem before the change worthless. What should it include?

options.text: The reassurance concerning prayers offered under the earlier direction
A claim that no early Muslims ever prayed
A suggestion that worshippers invented the original direction
A rule that every later preference changes revelation

questions.explanation: The report addresses this concern directly and recalls reassurance about the earlier prayers.

questions.question: A lawful community project becomes difficult, and volunteers can offer useful support. Which response draws a general lesson from Al-Miqdad's words?

options.text: Offer praise while refusing every agreed task
Share responsibility rather than leave one person with the whole challenge
Make support conditional on constant public admiration
Assume loyalty means accepting even unlawful instructions

questions.explanation: The modern comparison concerns dependable support. It does not turn the historical setting into a rule of blind obedience.

questions.question: A team assumes its large membership makes failure impossible. What reminder fits the account of Hunayn?

options.text: Large groups never need sound judgment
A setback proves no preparation should have been made
Numbers alone do not guarantee success
The biggest group is always protected from mistakes

questions.explanation: The verse recalls overconfidence in numbers followed by a setback, challenging certainty based on size alone.

questions.question: A lesson calls Hudaybiyyah nothing but defeat because some people initially found it difficult. How should it improve?

options.text: Ignore every report that challenges the first impression
Assume every unpopular agreement is automatically divinely approved
Treat negotiation as proof that no good outcome was possible
Include the reports identifying the agreement as a clear victory

questions.explanation: The reports correct a one-sided account. Their lesson does not grant modern agreements the Prophet's authority.

questions.question: Someone mocks a traveler for using a fasting concession when its conditions are properly met. Which Seerah reminder is relevant?

options.text: The Prophet himself used the travel concession
The Prophet forbade every traveler to use it
Residents and travelers always have identical circumstances
Using a valid concession necessarily rejects worship

questions.explanation: The report records the Prophet visibly breaking his fast on a journey. Individual circumstances still require the relevant guidance.

questions.question: A group wants a lawful optional change, but rushing it would needlessly unsettle people. What lesson fits the Kabah account?

options.text: Declare every optional improvement immediately compulsory
Consider consequences and explain the decision thoughtfully
Use the episode to ignore every duty
Assume wise timing is always cowardice

questions.explanation: The account illustrates considered restraint in a particular optional change, not permission to abandon obligations.

questions.question: A coordinator claims a good cause permits taking more than people properly owe. What lesson from Muadh's instructions applies?

options.text: Religious language cancels contributors' rights
The collector's personal preference determines every obligation
A good purpose does not remove safeguards against unfair taking
The most valuable possession is always owed automatically

questions.explanation: The instruction limits collection and warns against oppression. The scenario applies the principle of fair conduct, not zakah calculations.

questions.question: After a lawful distribution, long-serving members feel forgotten. Which response draws on the address to the Ansar?

options.text: Treat disappointment as proof that their service was worthless
Dismiss every concern without a conversation
Use warm words as permission to withhold what is actually owed
Listen, explain and acknowledge their contribution and belonging

questions.explanation: The Prophet addressed the Ansar's hurt and affirmed closeness. Reassurance should not become an excuse to deny genuine rights.

questions.question: A Seerah lesson describes the Farewell Hajj but ignores its warning about harming people. What should be restored?

options.text: The address's protection of life and property
The claim that pilgrimage excuses every later harm
A suggestion that ethics applies only outside worship
The idea that tribal rank permits taking others' belongings

questions.explanation: The account joins pilgrimage with moral responsibility. These protections belong in the lesson, not only the sequence of rites.

questions.question: Someone says their modern inconvenience permits inventing a new act of prescribed worship, just like the necklace incident. What distinction matters?

options.text: Every inconvenience grants the same authority as revelation
The incident involved revelation, not a rule invented by travelers
A lost object automatically replaces every religious duty
Any personal preference becomes prescribed if a group agrees

questions.explanation: The report describes Allah revealing the provision of tayammum. An ordinary later difficulty does not itself confer that authority.

questions.question: A child wants to tell you about a harmless interest that seems small to adults. Which response fits the Abu Umayr example?

options.text: Mock the interest as beneath adult dignity
Insist only important people's concerns deserve attention
Give warm, age-appropriate attention
Turn every conversation into a test of status

questions.explanation: The Prophet's approachable conversation about the bird shows attention to a child's ordinary world.

questions.question: A young learner needs help with an everyday practice. Which approach resembles the meal instruction?

options.text: Demand perfection without explaining any steps
Replace guidance with embarrassing comparisons
Assume a child can learn only through confusion
Give clear, manageable directions suited to the moment

questions.explanation: The remembered teaching was specific and usable. The example supports concrete guidance rather than a vague demand to behave better.

questions.question: An event thanks public speakers but overlooks the people who quietly maintain the space. What lesson fits the mosque-cleaner account?

options.text: Recognize quiet service rather than equating importance with visibility
Assume unseen work has no value
Thank only people with impressive titles
Treat modest duties as a reason for contempt

questions.explanation: The Prophet's regard for the cleaner challenges overlooking someone because their service lacks prestige.

questions.question: A community expresses sadness about genuine need but has not organized any assistance. Which next step fits Jarir's account?

options.text: Treat emotional words as the only possible response
Turn concern into appropriate, practical help
Discourage every suitable contribution
Wait until those in need become influential

questions.explanation: The account moves from visible concern to an appeal and gathered supplies, illustrating compassion put into action.

questions.question: A tribute assigns the Prophet a share in Allah's divinity to express love. Which correction follows his own instruction?

options.text: Treat affection as making every claim true
Assume praise cannot possibly cross a limit
Honor him as Allah's servant and messenger without that exaggeration
Say every expression of respect must stop

questions.explanation: The Prophet explicitly set limits on praise. Truthful honor follows his guidance rather than contradicting it.

questions.question: A lesson on the Prophet's death says love required denying that he had died. Which part of Abu Bakr's response should be included?

options.text: The claim that all duties ended with the death
A refusal to let Quranic guidance inform grief
The idea that messengership made human death impossible
Acknowledgment of the death while affirming the worship of the ever-living Allah

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr grieved yet recalled revelation and the distinction between Allah and His messenger. Love and acknowledgment of the death were not opposites.
